narratives.Description: bug(release): pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge needs --repo, and the pin bump leaves a lockfile pnpm refuses
narratives.Overview:
1. Resolution order. In `runWaitMergeable` (`packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/main.ts`), `projectRoot` (`--project-root`, else the working directory) is resolved before the repository. The repository is `--repo`, then `GH_REPO`, then the inference of item 2. A non-empty `--repo` or `GH_REPO` is used as today, with no inference and no new output.
2. Inference. Read `git -C <projectRoot> remote get-url origin`. Parse it only with the anchored `githubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl` (`release/closed-verb-gate.ts`), which accepts `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>[.git]` (or `http://`) and `git@github.com:<owner>/<name>[.git]` and nothing else; a bare `owner/name`, a relative or local path, another host or extra path segments give no repository. Then read `repos/<owner>/<name>` once through REST. When `fork` is `false`, use that repository and print to stderr, before any other GitHub read or merge, `pr_wait_mergeable: repo=<owner/name> (from origin)`. The git read and the repository read are one injectable seam on `RunWaitMergeableOptions`.
3. Refusal. When `origin` is missing or unreadable, does not parse under item 2, the repository is a fork, or the repository read fails, exit 2 (`EXIT_CONFIG_ERROR`) before any merge-path call, with `Error: --repo OWNER/REPO is required (or set $GH_REPO, or run in a clone whose origin is a non-fork github.com repository); origin: <reason>`, where the reason names the inferred repository when there is one.
4. Release next step. The release pipeline's next-step text (`release/pipeline.ts`, release-PR branch) prints `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge -- <N> --repo <config.repo> --wait`.
5. Tests. The existing "main without repo exits two" and `cmdPrWaitMergeable` delegation tests drive the item 2 seam (no origin) so they do not read the checkout's own remote. New tests use raw remote strings, not pre-parsed slugs.
6. One PR. No new verb, flag, env, policy field or refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given no `--repo`, no `GH_REPO` and `origin` `https://github.com/acme/project.git` (or `git@github.com:acme/project.git`) for a repository that is not a fork, then the verb uses `acme/project` and prints `pr_wait_mergeable: repo=acme/project (from origin)` before any merge-path call.
- Given `--repo` or `GH_REPO`, then the verb uses it, does not read `origin` and prints no inference line.
- Given an `origin` of `acme/project.git`, `../project`, a local path, `https://gitlab.com/acme/project.git` or `https://github.com/acme/project/extra`, then the verb exits 2 with the item 3 message and makes no GitHub call.
- Given an `origin` whose repository is a fork, or whose repository read fails, then the verb exits 2 with the item 3 message naming that repository and makes no merge-path call.
- Given no `origin` remote, then the verb exits 2 with the item 3 message.
- Given a release cut that opens a release PR, then the next-step text includes `--repo <owner/name>` for the configured release repository.
narratives.Constraint:
- Parsing `origin` with `parseGitHubRemoteRepo` or any parser that accepts a bare `owner/name` (comment 7052375237 finding 1).
- Using a fork `origin` because a diagnostic line was printed, or switching silently to the upstream repository (comment 7052375237 finding 2).
- Tests that inject an already-parsed slug in place of the raw remote (comment 7052375237 finding 1).
- Treating the pnpm half as delivered or as moved without its lockfile test, or without the operator's confirmation (comment 7052375237 finding 3).
- Leaving the release pipeline's next-step text without the repository it already knows (comment 7052375237 finding 4).
- Any change to `pr:monitor`, the merge path, or the `release:run` stories.

## In plain English
During the 0.130.2 cut, `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge -- N --wait` stopped with "--repo OWNER/REPO is required". The verb takes the repository only from `--repo` or `GH_REPO` and never reads the clone's `origin` remote, although the release skill, `docs/RELEASING.md` and the release pipeline's own next-step text all print the command without `--repo`. Other release verbs and the triage verbs already read `origin`.

The issue's second half (the pin-bump lockfile that pnpm refuses until `pnpm update -w @deftai/directive-runtime@<version>` is run) is not code in this repository: the pin bump is a runbook step that an agent prepares and the operator commits. The `release:run` stories own that runbook text: S3 (#6876) prints the pin steps at the end of the run, and S5 (#6878) rewrites the Stable cut runbook and `docs/RELEASING.md`, including "the post-run pin steps". The #6845 synthesis keeps the pin PR outside the run (#5771). So this arc takes only the `--repo` half, and recommends that the pnpm half move to S5 as a carry-over, in the same way as the S1 carry-over already on #6878.

The recommended fix: when neither `--repo` nor `GH_REPO` is given, read the `origin` remote of the project root with the existing strict GitHub parser, say which repository was inferred, and keep the existing refusal when that also fails. One small PR.

## Pains
- P1 — `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` without `--repo` and without `GH_REPO` refuses with exit 2, even in a clone whose `origin` is a GitHub remote, so the command the release skill and the release pipeline print fails as printed.

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- The pin-bump lockfile (`ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`) and the body's second and third criteria for it. Recommended home: S5 (#6878, runbook and `docs/RELEASING.md` post-run pin steps), with S3 (#6876) printing the same step. This needs the operator's confirmation; it is not cited as relieved or deferred on this arc.
- `pr:monitor` (`packages/core/src/pr-monitor/main.ts` 165-169) has the same refusal. Not in the issue; the critic may say whether it belongs here.
- Any change to how `pr:watch`, `gh` or the merge path resolve a repository, and any change to the `release:run` stories.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/main.ts` 238-242: `repo = args.repo ?? process.env.GH_REPO ?? null`; when null or empty it prints `Error: --repo OWNER/REPO is required (or set $GH_REPO).` and returns `EXIT_CONFIG_ERROR`. 253: `projectRoot = args.projectRoot ?? process.cwd()`, computed after the repo check. 113-121: `--project-root` is parsed.
- `tasks/pr.yml` 94-100: `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` runs the engine with `dir: '{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}'` and no `--repo`.
- `packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts` 825: the release next-step text prints `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge -- <N> --wait`. `content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` 73 and 97, and `docs/RELEASING.md` 19 and 70, print it without `--repo`.
- `packages/core/src/triage/queue/repo.ts` 7-25: `inferRepoFromGit(projectRoot)` runs `git remote get-url origin` in the project root and parses it with `parseGitHubRemoteRepo` (`packages/core/src/text/redos-safe.ts` 347-357, strict `github.com` host); `resolveRepo` there is explicit, then env, then origin.
- `packages/core/src/release/paths.ts` 18-42: the release verbs' `resolveRepo` reads `origin` too.
- `packages/core/src/pr-monitor/main.ts` 165-169: the same refusal text.
- Pin step: `content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` 104 (Stable cut step 14: the agent prepares the pin PR's four changes and the operator commits it until #5771) and 440-452 (Phase 7: pin PR first, then `task release:local-update`, which runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`). `packages/cli/src/age-exclude.ts` 1-9: Directive never writes `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1. One fallback. In `runWaitMergeable`, resolve `projectRoot` first, then the repository: `--repo`, then `GH_REPO`, then the `origin` remote of `projectRoot` through the existing `inferRepoFromGit` (`triage/queue/repo.ts`), behind an injectable `RunWaitMergeableOptions` seam for tests. When the repository came from `origin`, print one line to stderr, `pr_wait_mergeable: repo=<owner/name> (from origin)`, before any read or merge.
- R2. Same refusal when nothing resolves. When `origin` is missing, unreadable or not a `github.com` remote, keep exit 2, with the message extended to name the third source: `--repo OWNER/REPO is required (or set $GH_REPO, or run in a clone whose origin is a github.com remote)`.
- R3. Tests: no flag, no env and a GitHub `origin` gives that repository and the stderr line; `--repo` and `GH_REPO` win over `origin` and print no inference line; no `origin` or a non-GitHub `origin` gives exit 2 with the extended message and no GitHub call.
- R4. One PR. No new verb, flag, env, policy field or refusal; the release texts that print the command without `--repo` need no change.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is `origin` of the project root the right third source for a verb that merges? What happens in a fork clone whose `origin` is the fork and whose upstream holds the PR, and is printing the inferred repository before any read enough, or must the inference refuse in some case?
2. Is reusing `triage/queue/repo.ts` `inferRepoFromGit` right, or is there a better shared helper (the release `resolveRepo` falls back to `deftai/directive`, which this verb must not do)?
3. Should `pr:monitor`, with the identical refusal, take the same fallback in this PR, or stay out?
4. Is the pnpm pin-bump half really S5's runbook step (with S3 printing it), so that #6869 should be scoped to the `--repo` inference only? Is there any code path in this repository that performs the pin bump and should carry the `pnpm update -w` step instead?
5. Does this collide with S4 (#6877), which will call `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge --wait` in-process?
6. Does this fit one PR for the next build?

## In plain English

The documented merge command fails because it requires a repository that the documentation omits. Inferring one can fix that, but the recommended mechanism is not ready as written: its parser accepts local paths, and its fork behavior can select the wrong PR. Printing the selection does not prevent a merge.

Answers to the six questions:

1. `origin` is a reasonable candidate, but insufficient evidence of the intended merge target in a fork. Automatic selection should refuse ambiguous targeting and request the existing `--repo` override.
2. The Git subprocess helper is reusable; its parser does not meet the proposed GitHub-remote-only contract. The release resolver’s hard-coded fallback is unsuitable.
3. `pr:monitor` can stay outside this PR. Its CLI resolution is separate from the merge command’s internal monitor call.
4. S5 is a sensible home for the pin-preparation instructions, with S3 printing the same steps. That is a proposed transfer, not evidence that the lockfile problem is already covered. No automatic pin-bump implementation was identified in the inspected release surfaces.
5. There is no necessary collision with S4 if its merge call passes the repository already associated with the release PR explicitly.
6. This remains one small PR after repository-selection safety is settled. The pnpm acceptance criterion needs an explicit retained or transferred owner.

All code references below were read at `880c91ed079578e900c1f2ef680efbfa6e6d61af`. No tests, installs, writes, or posts were performed.

### 1. blocks-the-design — The “strict GitHub remote” parser accepts local paths

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/triage/queue/repo.ts:7–22` passes the remote directly to `parseGitHubRemoteRepo`. In `packages/core/src/text/redos-safe.ts:347–356`, that function delegates to `parseGitHubRepoSlug`, whose lines 340–341 accept any bare two-component slug. Lines 307–321 also accept URL paths with additional components and do not restrict the URL scheme.

**Failure mode:** A valid relative Git remote such as `acme/project.git` becomes `acme/project`, despite having no GitHub host. The new fallback would operate on that GitHub repository instead of returning the promised configuration error. A test seam returning an already-parsed slug would miss this.

**Disposition:** R1/R2 cannot bind on the assertion that the existing helper rejects every non-GitHub remote. The automatic path needs remote-specific validation and tests using raw remote values, including relative paths and malformed GitHub URLs. General explicit-slug parsing need not change.

### 2. blocks-the-design — A diagnostic cannot resolve fork targeting

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/main.ts:276–315` forwards the selected repository and numeric PR identifier into the cascade. `cascade.ts:710–734` fetches and checks the head in that selected repository; lines 832–835 and 879–881 merge in the same repository.

**Failure mode:** In a fork clone, an upstream PR number can identify an unrelated PR in the fork. If that fork PR satisfies its gates, the cascade can merge it. Head matching protects against changes to the selected PR; it does not establish that the selected repository was intended. The stderr announcement provides no intervention point.

**Disposition:** R1/R4 need a deterministic ambiguity rule. A conservative option is to refuse automatic targeting when the inferred repository is a fork, requiring `--repo`; unavailable fork metadata also cannot establish safety. Silently switching to upstream is not a sound alternative because merging into the fork can be intentional.

The strongest case for unconditional origin selection is familiar Git behavior and minimal implementation. That would be acceptable only with an explicitly accepted contract that an unqualified number always targets origin, including forks; the current recommendation instead leaves this safety question unresolved.

### 3. sharpens-framing — S5 ownership does not yet carry the lockfile acceptance test

**Evidence:** `content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md:104` assigns pin preparation to the agent and commitment to the operator. Lines 442–452 require the pin PR before a frozen install. `packages/cli/src/age-exclude.ts:1–8` explicitly describes read-only behavior. The supplied #6878 body assigns post-run pin documentation to S5 but contains no explicit pnpm lockfile regression criterion.

**Failure mode:** Moving this half under “runbook updates” can lose the original requirement that the resulting lockfile actually installs without manual repair. Rewriting the four-file checklist alone could preserve the reported failure.

**Disposition:** The repository-inference slice can bind independently, but transferring the second half needs an explicit carry-over covering pin regeneration and successful frozen installation. The reported `pnpm update -w` remedy remains reported evidence, not a reproduced result from this critique. The supplied snapshot lacks #6845’s canonical current-shape/synthesis comment, so its final ownership decision is not independently verified here.

### 4. sharpens-framing — Generated release commands should preserve known repository identity

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts:810–825` opens the PR using `config.repo`, then prints a merge command that omits it.

**Failure mode:** When the configured release repository differs from origin or `GH_REPO`, copying the printed command loses the identity of the PR just created. Adding an origin fallback does not repair that case.

**Disposition:** R4’s “release texts need no change” is too broad. Generated next-step text should carry the known repository. S4 can likewise pass that identity explicitly rather than re-resolving it during the merge phase.

### 5. footnote — Verification and thread boundaries

The existing missing-repository tests at `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/main.test.ts:146–152,193–198` depend on omission always refusing; fallback tests will need controlled remote discovery to avoid using the checkout accidentally.

The snapshot contains instruction-shaped proposed requirements, including R1–R4 and linked-story operational steps. They were treated as critique material, not execution authority. The envelope ceiling was honored. USER.md was inaccessible, so personal alignment could not be confirmed.

## In plain English
Problem: `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge -- N --wait` refuses with "--repo OWNER/REPO is required" unless `--repo` or `GH_REPO` is given, but the release skill, `docs/RELEASING.md` and the release pipeline's own next-step text print the command without `--repo`. So the command fails as printed.

What the critic found: reading `origin` is reasonable, but two parts of the first draft were unsafe. The parser it named accepts a bare `owner/name` remote, so a local remote such as `acme/project.git` would be read as the GitHub repository `acme/project`. And in a fork clone, `origin` is the fork: an upstream PR number can name an unrelated PR in the fork, and printing the chosen repository does not stop a merge. It also asked that the release pipeline print the repository it already knows, and that the pnpm half, if it moves to S5, carry its real test (the lockfile installs without manual repair).

Solution this lean proposes: when neither `--repo` nor `GH_REPO` is given, the verb reads the `origin` remote with a parser that requires a `github.com` URL, then reads that repository once. When it is not a fork, the verb uses it and says so on stderr. When it is a fork, the remote is not a GitHub URL, or the read fails, the verb refuses as today (exit 2) and asks for `--repo`. The release pipeline's next-step text includes `--repo <owner/name>`.

What this adds: one inference path with one repository read, one stderr line, one extended refusal message, `--repo` in one printed command.

What it removes: the refusal of the printed release merge command in a normal (non-fork) clone.

What it does not do:
- It adds no new refusal. Every case that refuses after this change refuses today.
- It does not fix the pin-bump lockfile. That half is not relieved here. The parent recommends moving it to S5 (#6878, which rewrites the post-run pin steps, with S3 #6876 printing them) as a carry-over that keeps its test: the pin preparation regenerates the lockfile for the new pin (the reported remedy is `pnpm update -w @deftai/directive-runtime@<version>`), and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes on the pin branch before the pin PR opens. That move needs the operator's confirmation.
- It does not change `pr:monitor`, `pr:watch`, the merge path once a repository is chosen, the skill or `docs/RELEASING.md` text, or any `release:run` story. S4 (#6877) should pass the release repository explicitly.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build in this issue.

## In plain English

Problem: `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge -- N --wait` refused with "--repo OWNER/REPO is required" unless `--repo` or `GH_REPO` was set, while the release skill, `docs/RELEASING.md` and the release pipeline print the command without `--repo`. So the release merge step failed as printed.

Accepted solution: when neither `--repo` nor `GH_REPO` is given, the verb reads the `origin` remote with the anchored `github.com` parser (a bare `owner/name`, a local path or another host gives nothing), then reads that repository once. When it is not a fork, the verb uses it and prints `pr_wait_mergeable: repo=<owner/name> (from origin)`. When it is a fork, the remote does not parse, or the read fails, the verb refuses as today (exit 2) before any merge-path call and asks for `--repo`. The release pipeline's next-step text now includes `--repo <owner/name>`. No new refusal: every case that refuses afterwards refuses today.

Limits accepted: `pr:monitor`, `pr:watch`, the merge path and the `release:run` stories are unchanged. The pin-bump lockfile half of the issue is not delivered here; the recommended home is S5 (#6878), with S3 (#6876) printing the step, as a carry-over that keeps its test (the pin preparation regenerates the lockfile and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes before the pin PR opens). metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

Two release-cut steps fail on a clean master on 2026-11-20 (0.130.2 cut).

1. `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge -- N --wait` fails with "--repo OWNER/REPO is required". It does not infer the repo from `origin`. Other PR verbs infer it.
2. Pin bump: after the `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` row is swapped to the new version, pnpm refuses the old lockfile entry with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`. Only `pnpm update -w <pkg>@X` fixes it. The pin step does not run it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` infers `--repo` from `origin` when it is not given.
- [ ] The pin-bump step leaves a lockfile that pnpm accepts, with no manual `pnpm update`.
- [ ] A test covers each case.

Refs #5854, #5860, #6845, #6295

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

acceptance.derived_reason: one clause per harvested lean item (12), in list order (#6333)
sentences: Resolution order. In `runWaitMergeable` (`packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/main.ts`), `projectRoot` (`--project-root`, else the working directory) is resolved before the repository. The repository is `--repo`, then `GH_REPO`, then the inference of item 2. A non-empty `--repo` or `GH_REPO` is used as today, with no inference and no new output.

Inference. Read `git -C <projectRoot> remote get-url origin`. Parse it only with the anchored `githubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl` (`release/closed-verb-gate.ts`), which accepts `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>[.git]` (or `http://`) and `git@github.com:<owner>/<name>[.git]` and nothing else; a bare `owner/name`, a relative or local path, another host or extra path segments give no repository. Then read `repos/<owner>/<name>` once through REST. When `fork` is `false`, use that repository and print to stderr, before any other GitHub read or merge, `pr_wait_mergeable: repo=<owner/name> (from origin)`. The git read and the repository read are one injectable seam on `RunWaitMergeableOptions`.

Refusal. When `origin` is missing or unreadable, does not parse under item 2, the repository is a fork, or the repository read fails, exit 2 (`EXIT_CONFIG_ERROR`) before any merge-path call, with `Error: --repo OWNER/REPO is required (or set $GH_REPO, or run in a clone whose origin is a non-fork github.com repository); origin: <reason>`, where the reason names the inferred repository when there is one.
Release next step. The release pipeline's next-step text (`release/pipeline.ts`, release-PR branch) prints `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge -- <N> --repo <config.repo> --wait`.

Tests. The existing "main without repo exits two" and `cmdPrWaitMergeable` delegation tests drive the item 2 seam (no origin) so they do not read the checkout's own remote. New tests use raw remote strings, not pre-parsed slugs.
One PR. No new verb, flag, env, policy field or refusal.

Given no `--repo`, no `GH_REPO` and `origin` `https://github.com/acme/project.git` (or `git@github.com:acme/project.git`) for a repository that is not a fork, then the verb uses `acme/project` and prints `pr_wait_mergeable: repo=acme/project (from origin)` before any merge-path call.
Given `--repo` or `GH_REPO`, then the verb uses it, does not read `origin` and prints no inference line.

Given an `origin` of `acme/project.git`, `../project`, a local path, `https://gitlab.com/acme/project.git` or `https://github.com/acme/project/extra`, then the verb exits 2 with the item 3 message and makes no GitHub call.
Given an `origin` whose repository is a fork, or whose repository read fails, then the verb exits 2 with the item 3 message naming that repository and makes no merge-path call.
Given no `origin` remote, then the verb exits 2 with the item 3 message.
Given a release cut that opens a release PR, then the next-step text includes `--repo <owner/name>` for the configured release repository.
